chapter: Paris scene and a visit home, 1937-39
title: Pigalle's expatriates: Mabel Mercer, Opal Cooper, Juice Wilson
summary: He lists Americans playing in Pigalle, Bricktop's with Mabel Mercer, singer Opal Cooper, Glover Compton, Arthur Lanier and violinist Juice Wilson, who stayed too long in Algeria.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: There was entertainment everywhere and now Pigalle, you had and Bricktop had a place in Pigalle, and Mabel Mercer was singing there. That's the last time I saw her. She was singing that beautiful stuff and another place called Melody's Bar. You had a jazz band in there and you had a man named Opal Cooper. Well, Opal Cooper could outsing Caruso. After he lost all his money, he was out singing.

Opal Cooper, I think he was from Chicago. Then you had Glover Compton and all these fellows -- they had them from all around. They had a bunch of fellows who come out from Spain. They had their Spanish women but a boy named Chase, he come from Washington and one man named Mufflejaws Mars, he come from Washington, D. C. and sure, they was there too, and we would all meet Arthur Laniers also, then you had one fellow who was a jazz violin player named Juice Wilson. He was a violin player, I mean

he was a champ. He stayed in Algeria but he stayed too long. He lost all his finger on the fiddle but he played saxophone. He was something special. See, what happened, the guy had stayed -- he went over there as a young man with a show or something, and he stayed and then he didn't care about keeping up on his instrument. He became of the country where he lived and then you had Englishmen coming over --
